items.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Ed Bickert was a dear friend and marvelous guitar player, who ended up playing with Desmond and everything.

ctx.x: Bourbon Street, yeah. And I would always take a bass player from New York or something with me. And then, I went to… Ed Bickert was a dear friend and marvelous guitar player, who ended up playing with Desmond and everything. I went over to Ed’s house once for a jam session and Don Thompson and Terry Clarke were there, and I said, “Why am I take… bringing musicians from New York?” So… we… I’ve worked with Don and Terry. That’s how we hooked up. And Don just put recording equipment on the stage, and we were there…
and we all crack up, and that’s because we… I didn’t even realize we were recording or I had forgotten. But it came out really nice, I think.
